The respondent is a fire investigator and is reporting an incident that was brought to his attention by a consumer who owned the product in this report.  The respondent does not physically own the product and has not seen it, but in light of the recent recall CAP# 11-255, he wanted to report these details to the CPSC.

The respondent stated that the consumer reported that she was outside using the fuel gel in a firepot on her patio , she then tried to refuel it, however, the content exploded on her causing her to receive 2nd and 3rd degree burns to her upper body which including face, arms, hands and chest.  She was taken to a burn Center at the University hospital, 602 Indiana Ave, Lubbock Tx 79415,  where she was admitted for several days.  She was then released and sent home where she is currently recuperating.

There is a Fire report - [REDACTED].

The manufacturer has not been contacted.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns (2nd and 3rd degree) and hospitalization, but no fatalities were reported.

incident_description:
My wife was burned over 60-75% of her body when our friend used the Napa brand citronella fire gel.
The gel was ejected from the bottle and flew  approximately 8 feet before the burning fuel struck my wife. My wife did not initially realize she was on fire because she could not see the flame. She attempted to stop, drop and roll.  When she stood up, the gel re-ignited.  It took 4-6 friends to help get the fire out on the second stop, drop and roll attempt.  She was flown by helicopter to the Washington Hospital Center burn unit where she was admitted to the ICU.  She remains hospitalized after 76 days.
justification: The severity level is 3 due to significant injuries, and the occurrence likelihood is 3 as such incidents, while possible, are not common.

incident_description:
http://www.cpsc.gov/cpscpub/prerel/prhtml98/98094.html


Elite Lighter malfunctioned and the flint flew out upon the first light. 

Also, the lighter stayed lit after I wished to extinguish the flame. 

I bought the darn thing at Walgreens on Apalachee PKWY in Tallahassee, FL
justification: The lighter malfunctioned, causing the flint to fly out and the flame to stay lit after the user attempted to extinguish it, posing a potential burn hazard.

incident_description: I was at my friend [REDACTED]'s house in Arizona on July 3, 2011. She had a fire pot using Napa fire gel fuel manufactured by Napa Home and Garden. The fire pot had been burning for a few hours and then once the gel was depleted and the flame had gone out, she went to refill the firepot approximately 15-20 minutes later. Not a second after she began to refill the firepot, there was a huge explosion. I just remember a huge ball of fire in my face. The next thing I remember was standing in my friend's kitchen with her and another friend holding ice packs and wet towels on my arm. I was extremely upset and in shock. Once I was a little calmer my friend explained that I caught on fire. They said that I took off running and that they had to push me to the ground and rolled me in the dirt until the fire was out. They also had to rip my shirt off as it was also in flames. My arm was severely burned, the blisters were huge and covered most of my right arm. My hair had also been burnt badly. All I could smell was burnt hair and skin.  I was in excruciating pain. Once at the ER I was told that I had severe 2nd degree burns. My throat had also been burnt and I had several blisters in the back of my throat. It has now been one month and the burns are almost healed, but there are still some scabs and deep scarring.
justification: The incident resulted in severe 2nd degree burns, throat burns, and deep scarring, making it a '3 - Injury' on the severity scale. The likelihood is '4 - likely' as the refilling process triggered an unexpected explosion.

incident_description:
On February 16, 2011, my husband and I were sitting on our patio.  We poured Napa fuel gel into our fire pot and lit it.  We sat the bottle of gel about a foot away from the pot.  (We don't remember if the top was on or off the bottle.)  All of the sudden, the bottle exploded.  The gel that passed over the open flame of the pot ignited and landed on me.  (It sounded like a gun shot.)  The flash sunburned my face, synged my eyelashes, and burned my left ear.  It caught my left arm, back, hair and shirt on fire.  My husband tackled me with a blanket to extinguish the flames.  I threw up, passed out and went into shock.  We went to the emergency room, and the next day to a burn center at a hosptial.  That day I went into surgery where they scrapped my skin.  I had first and second degree burns and was out of work from February 17th-March 4th.  

My concern is that I was NOT pouring the gel into an open flame, or an empty, hot resevior when it combusted, like MANY stories I have heard.  I fear more people/pets/homes will be injured/ruined if the fire pots and fuel gel remain on the shelves of stores.
justification: The incident resulted in significant injuries, including first and second degree burns, and the likelihood of similar incidents occurring is high given the widespread use of these products.

incident_description: The consumer says he filled the gas tank but it wont work on the bbq grill.  He says gas leaks from it posing a fire hazard.  The consumer says there is a universal cylinder that is supposed to work on all gas tanks but not when using the grill.  He says this is a newer cylinder where he does not need a wrench to spin it.  He says he has only had it filled 4 or 5 times.  The next time he filled it is when he had a leak in it.  he says the local gas company and says they filled it the same way they have been doing and did not look any different.  The product is similar to a 1997 recall for the same company under Release # 97-174, however the consumer's valve is much older.
justification: Potential fire hazard due to gas leak, though no injuries reported yet.

incident_description:
Was filling a lawn tractor gas tank from a 5 gallon plastic container equipped with automatic fill tube. When I put the weight of the tank on the fill tube end to actuate the automatic filling the outer part of the tube suddenly came off and entered the tractor's gas tank. Since the 5 gallon container was inverted large amounts of gas splashed all over the tractor and also myself. The quickest thing I could think was to continue filling the tractor tank rather than have the gas splashing around. When the tractor tank was full there was still about 2 gallons of gas in the container. I had to remove and  invert the container as quickly as possible which I did. When I was through I had spilled a large quanity of gas on the tractor, on my hands and clothing an on the ground. Fortunately no fire occured but the outer tube and other parts are in the tractor gas tank and th 5 gallon container is useless for gas.
    Briggs & Stratton 5 gallon gas container Model # 528. The following statements are on in the container,     "SPILL PROOF SYSTEM"
                   "SMART FILL FUELING SYSTEM"
                   " Briggs & Stratton Logo"
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant fuel spillage, rendering the gas container and possibly the tractor's fuel system unusable.

incident_description:
After placing the nozzle of the container into the lawn mowers gas tank he noticed that gasoline began to leak out onto his hands, the ground and some even splashed into his eyes. 

At the tip of the nozzle there is a safety cap that has to inserted inside of the gas tank and when lifting the container it causes the gas to leak out.  He indicated that itÃÂs a major safety concern and someone could possibly be injured with gas leaking on them, or on a hot engine.

The manufacturer has not been contacted, nor the retailer but he plans to contact the firm.  He currently has two of the 2 gallon containers and uses them not so often, after removing the so-called "safety nozzles."
justification: Gasoline splashed into his eyes, posing a high risk of injury.

incident_description: I was sitting at a patio table around 9pm when an emptied fire pot was about to be refilled with the lighter gel (Patio glo) Before the gel even came out of the bottle, the gel exploded into a ball of fire and blew me backwards where I lay on fire. I ended up with 2nd degree burns on my face, arms, chest, stomach and back.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries (2nd degree burns) and could have been catastrophic.

incident_description:
I purchased a Briggs & Stratton 85053 - 5 Gallon Plastic Spill Proof Gas Can 
for my boat.  It worked twice and then failed.  It leaked gas on my hands, on my boat, and in the water.  This is a hazard to me and to the environment.

incident_description:
THE LIGHTNING BOLT TROPICAL FISH 7 SHOT FIRE WORK LB-B043 SHOT OUT THE SIDE OF THE FIREWORK ON TWO OF THE SEVEN SHOTS, ONE SHOT INTO A CROWD OF KIDS AND THE OTHER SHOT INTO MYSELF AND LIT MY SHIRT AND COMPLETELY BURNED THE TOP SHIRT AND SECOND SHIRT UNDERNEATH, INCLUDING THE BLANKET CAUGHT ON FIRE.
GROUP OF FAMILY WAS SITTING OVER 50 YDS AWAY FROM FIREWORKS THAT WERE BEING LIT IN MIDDLE OF THE STREET, WE WERE SITTING ON FRONT LAWN OF HOME.
justification: Injury occurred due to a firework malfunction, shooting into a crowd and setting the victim's clothing on fire.

incident_description:
A friend of the husband and wife purchased fuel gel at Wal-Mart (Birdbrain brand) along with the "Firepot" from an internet 
website.  The husband and wife were sitting on the other side of a picnic table talking.  The friend who had purchased the fuel pot and gel had commented that the fuel gel doesn't last very long and it was expensive.  They had been talking and the pot had burned out/used up the fuel and the friend went to get the fuel gel container.  The friend, on the other side of the picnic table from the husband and wife, poured the gel into the pot and flames shot out immediately and towards and on to the husband and wife.  They were on fire and were rolling on the ground and trying to put out the flames.  The wife's hair was on fire as well.  The wife received first, second and possibly third degree or deep partial thickness burns to her face and arm while the husband received first and second degree burns to his arm.  The tablecloth burned and was thrown away because the friend was so traumatized.
justification: The incident resulted in severe burns to both the husband and wife, with the wife suffering potentially life-altering injuries, making it a '3 - Injury' on the severity scale. The likelihood is '4 - almost certain' given the immediate and unexpected reaction of the fuel gel when poured into the pot.

incident_description:
On 7/24/11, we purchased a couple of fireworks from the "Olympus Firework" stand on [REDACTED], in West Jordan, Utah. All proper safety instructions and precautions were followed by us. The first firework we lit was an aerial firework called "picture perfect" one of the first blast blew out the bottom of the firework and each subsequent shot sent the blast at ground level. After each shot the firework would spin so it was impossible to predict where the next shoot was going to shot. We had shots under a car, in a garage, one landed in a grass and started a small fire, then we had one shoot into a crowd of small children and their parents.

The children and all involved were rightfully terrified and traumatized by the experience. We are lucky no one was seriously hurt and there was no property damage caused.  However, after that experience I feel this firework is extremely unsafe and should be recalled immediately. No, specific victims are identified in this report, other than myself, because in this report because there were 28 people there, including 13 adults and 15 children(most under the age of 10).  

We did return the spent firework and the remaining fireworks we purchased to the stand on [REDACTED]. Those who were operating the firework stand were kind, showed concern and refunded our money. The operators did imply it may have been caused by the firework getting wet at their stand. I appreciate their attempt to explain why this happened, however it only caused concern that they would continue to sell fireworks that were exposed to conditions that could make them so dangers. Ether way the firework is dangerously defective or fireworks are being sold the have been exposed to conditions that make them unsafe.
justification: Despite safety precautions, the firework's defective behavior caused panic and trauma, but no serious injuries.

incident_description:
I purchased   MiniMatch butane lighters at a CVS store on July 16, 2011  The flame that shoots out of the lighter is hugh.  At the lowest setting it was about 2 inches high and at the High setting about 3 inches high.  This product is from Calico Brands, Inc.   Ontario, California 91761

I think this is unsafe for a cigarette lighter   the flame is too high  I could have burned my nose or eyebrows if I wasn't diligent.

incident_description:
We purchased ten Islander Tiki brand torches at a local true value hardware store, during an end of season sale late last year. Two of these torches, caught fire July 5, 2011. The fire melted both the plastic container and the holding basket, which mounts atop a wooden pole.   We used Tike brand citronella liquid as recommended by the manufacturer. 

The description of our purchase included a 4 to 5 ft. pole with a woven basket mounted atop it, a plastic holding container and a screw on metal lid that contains a fiberglass wick. The label claim stated "Paradise in Your Backyard" and "Trusted by Millions?" 

My husband and I stepped into our house, for a period of not more than 6-10 minutes, to make a sandwich and grab some refreshment to bring back outside with us. The torches were located along an 80 ft. long versa block retaining wall. Suddenly, through a window, we saw smoke billowing. 
We ran outside as quickly as possible and saw 2 - 3 ft. high flames.  

The ground around the torches was ablaze; a complete melt down occurred.  The plastic bottled was 100% melted as was the woven basket mounted atop the pole. Poof Gone!!!! The ground saturated with flaming liquid from the torches.  My husband received a minor burn attempting to smother the flames with a towel. I ran for a garden hose somewhere in the process I received a minor cut on my hand. In this brief period, the fire spread rapidly roughly a span of 4 - 5ft. and began to singe my shrubbery. The citronella liquid acted as a catalyst when absorbed in the ground below. 

Furthermore, it caused damage to our retaining walls 120v electrical supply, which also caught fire.  The conduit and inner wiring melted along with the entire GFI box and outlet. The melt down was so severe the receptacle fell out completely. The damage sustained to the electrical conduit is 2 ft. in length above the ground; however, we do not know the extent of the underground damage to the conduit and wiring. Currently the circuit breakers are cutoff to avoid any electrical shock. In additionally, a low voltage lighting system has also damaged in the incident. We have an electrician coming over to provide an estimate for the damages sustained due to the poor design of these Tiki Brand Torches, made in China, for Lamplight Farms, Inc. 

Prior to the fire, my back yard was a paradise of lovely plantings and a pond containing a double waterfall. Now my pond does not work due to loss of electric within the retaining wall. Would you call this Paradise?
justification: Injuries occurred due to the rapid spread of fire caused by the citronella liquid acting as a catalyst, and the poor design of the torches.

incident_description:
Consumer wanted to report that his Blitz cans are potentially hazardous. Consumer stated that the gas can are 5 gallons and plastic. The compressor valve is spring loaded The consumer stated that the issue with the gas can is when a person tries to depress the valve to fill up the lawn mower with gasoline, the gasoline flows out from underneath the valve handle and spills. This happened to the consumer twice with two different identical gas cans. In the first instance the gas can spill gasoline all over the consumer's leg and on a hot lawn mower. The second incident happened a couple weeks later with another identical gas can. The consumer feels that a person could go up in flames if this problem persists. The consumer was not injured during the incident but still notices a potential danger in this issue. The consumer has yet to call the manufacturer but did take the product back to the Wal Mart yesterday for a refund. The consumer stated that there was no fire or flames. The consumer cannot recall the date of the incident. The consumer felt it was imperative 
to report this issue to the CPSC.
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the potential for severe burns or fire is high due to gasoline spills near heat sources.

incident_description:
I recently purchased a 3-pack of Scripto stick-type lighters (Calico Brands, inc., Ontario CA 917610. Well, the buttons stick and sometimes the flame keeps burning after theyÃÂre set down. With one lighter, the flame went out but all of the flammable gas exhausted itself and I had to throw it away after only one day.

On Saturday, June 25, 2011, I had a couple over for an outdoor barbeque, and one of my friends used the Scripto lighter on the table to light a cigarette, and didnÃÂt realize the button was stuck and it was still throwing a flame. We all went in the house, and unbeknownst to us, the tablecloth caught fire and severely scorched my antique wooden table, the value of which  is (was) probably well over $500.00.

Here in New Mexico, forest fires are raging out of control; high winds, high temperatures and no rain! I live around horse ranches and hay barns. This could easily have started a neighborhood fire, I live in Santa Fe, right next to the big Pacheco fire currently in progress.

Two of the lighters have the code JX 11 2, and the third is JX 09. I believe this problem with the lighters has to do with the childproof feature, which, any three-year old could figure out. This needs to be made public knowledge before someone inadvertently starts a house fire or a forest fire.

[redacted]
justification: Although no injuries occurred, the incident resulted in significant property damage (scorched antique wooden table valued at over $500) and posed a high likelihood of spreading to nearby hay barns and contributing to the ongoing Pacheco fire.

incident_description:
Caller is Florida State Fire Investigator and is reporting a fire with injuries as a result of the pourable Eco-Gel being burned for illuminated lighting the evening of June 3, 2011.
The female victim was refilling the container with the pourable gel (caller is not sure whether the container was still lit or whether fire in container being filled had gone out already).
While refilling the gel the container exploded burning both the female filling it and her husband were burned.
Wife was burned approximately 70% of her body with first, second and third degree burns over her face, upper body and legs and her husband suffered first and second degree burns over approximately 10% of his body involving his legs and hands.
Wife was transported by ambulance to the hospital emergency room while husband rode in the ambulance with her and both were seen in the emergency room.
Wife was admitted into the hospital then airlifted to another hospital with burn unit where she remains at this date.
Husband was treated and released.
Damages to victim's condominium are estimated at approximately $5,000.
Caller is obligated to report this product as a state employee investigating the fire.
justification: Injuries occurred due to the volatile nature of the pourable Eco-Gel when mishandled, and the likelihood is high given the product's widespread use and lack of clear safety instructions.

incident_description:
Was sitting at my computer out on my deck with a firepot lit on my coffee table. The silver canister inside my ceramic bowl shot out of the bowl and landed on the other side of the love seat where I was sitting. It spread fire along it's path dropping it on the love seat cushions, table, my computer, rug and also my leg, hand and top of head was on fire.
My husband came right away and put out my head, threw me in the house and put out my hand and leg. I have 2nd degree burns to my right leg between the knee and ankle. 
I have used the firepot many times after getting it for Mother's Day. But this is the first time I used the citronella gel. It happened with 10 minutes of lighting it. I did nothing different this time then I have in the past and I followed the directions.
I loved my pot but these are tooo unstable to use. These must be recalled right away. I am very lucky that I was not hurt worse and that my pets and children were not outside with me!
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns, and the likelihood of occurrence is high given the instability of the firepot with citronella gel.

incident_description:

                          UPC=  044549810102    " AND ALL OTHERS WITH THIS DESIGN "

These plastic gasoline cans have NO vent or pressure relief so they swell and expand
causing several problems;

     The company should be ashamed of itself producing such a dangerous, awkward to use, piece of junk.

incident_description: In Madison, AL on May 29 2011 around 8:00pm CST, a ceramic fuel pot was lit while a family lounged in the backyard of the victim's house.  Due to a lack of fuel gel, the flame quickly died down and more fuel gel was then poured into the pot.  Once the gel touched the fire pot, it immediately ignited and exploded, spraying onto the face, neck, and upper torso of the victim.  The flaming gel stuck to the front of the victim's body as his shirt and skin went up in flames.  This caused first, second and third degree burns to over 40% of his body.  The manufacturer of the firepot fuel gel is BirdBrain.  The product is called BirdBrain Firepot Fuel Gel.  Its product number is SKU 391380508. The fuel gel was purchased from Big Lots.
justification: The incident resulted in severe injuries (first, second, and third-degree burns over 40% of the body), hence severity level 3. The likelihood is high as the incident occurred due to a common action (adding fuel) and involved a widely available product, making it likely to happen again.

incident_description: On May 29, 2011, I was pouring fire gel into my new frie bowl and when I lit I didn't see the flame, and I realized I had not put enough gel into the bowl, so as I was pouring some more the fuel in the bottle exploded and it kind of went everywhere.  So I sat the bowl down, within seconds, my brother who was sitting within two to three feet from me, shoes caught on fire.  I tried to fan the fire off his feet and within seconds it had caught his pants and the fire was up to his waist.  While we were trying to put the fire out on him, my sandals caught on fire and within seconds, the fire was up my legs.  Both of us sustained second degree burns.
justification: Both individuals sustained second-degree burns, indicating a severe injury (severity level 3). The rapid progression of the fire and its spread to both individuals suggests a high likelihood of occurrence (4).

incident_description: On April 30, I attended a supper club where we were visiting at a patio table on the host and hostesses back patio.  The hostess had a beautiful ceramic pot which she had received as a wedding gift.  The pot was filled with a gel fuel made by Napa Fire.  The "candle" fuel burned down during the evening and she refilled it later in the evening.  Upon refilling it, the fuel exploded into a fireball which hit me in my face and must have rolled down my body.  I was so concerned about my face that I did not realize that my left leg was on fire.  My husband and the host threw me to the ground and rolled me while slapping the fire out on my leg.  By the grace of God, my face did not burn and I washed and washed the gel off my face, out of my eyes, and out of my mouth.  I was absolutely distraught and it was the scariest thing that ever happened to me.  As I did go into shock, my husband took me on to our local hospital, Spartanburg Regional, and they treated my burns on my legs which were only 2nd degree burns and not 3rd degree.  We and all the guests assumed it was a freak accident until another friend was terribly burned in Spartanburg, SC about 4 weeks later and airlifted to the Augusta Burn Center in Georgia.  We also have been contacted that another lady from Greenville, SC was terribly burned at the beginning of May by the same product when her husband was filling the pot.  She also had to go to the Augusta Burn center.  Please, please get this terrible product off the market!  It is being sold in so many gift stores and markets.  In my situation it was a small pot.  I have heard there are very large ones and cannot imagine the damage they will do to someone.
justification: The incident resulted in second-degree burns and potential for severe harm, and similar incidents have occurred recently with the same product.

Another person at the table lit a lighter (it was about 6-8 inches from the pot) and the gel exploded out, caught the flame and a fire ball came at me and caught my front side on fire, including my hair. My daughter filled one resevoir then the other and when my son in law attempted to light it using a match it ignited/erupted and spewed flaming gel fuel!!

incident_description: My Wedco gas can which I had for about 1 year developed a hole in its lower corner. Due to the new "spill proof" nozzle design, the can isn't able to be properly vented while not in use. As a result the corner collapses in on itself. incident_description:
My name is [REDACTED]. I am a Captain/Fire Investigator for the Omaha Fire Department. Below I will detail an incident that I believe the CPSC should be aware of.

Friday June 3rd, 2011 2159 hours, The Omaha Fire Department was dispatched to an incident of persons burned. Upon arrival Omaha Fire Personnel find three adults and one child burned, the child and two of the adults sustained severe burn injuries and were transported to the area trauma center.

An investigation into the Incident determined a family was having a gathering on their deck. The three most severely injured were seated on a love seat type, glider rocker. Located on a patio table approximately six feet away were two ceramic "Firepots" containing a gel type fuel. The products are specifically described as "Napa Firelite Party Time, Glazed Ceramic, 5 Inch by 4 3/4 Inch Square" and "NAPAFire Eco Gel Fuel - 32oz by Napa Home". According to one of the victims, who was seated near the "Firepots", one of the "Firepots" appeared to have extinguished itself by utilizing all of the "Gel Fuel". The victim stated as he was attempting to pour more "Gel Fuel" from the 32oz bottle into the stainless dish within the Ceramic "Firepot", the bottle exploded, spraying the burning "Gel Fuel" all over the three victims that were seated together.

It was noted that the NAPAfire EcoGel Fuel is in a container similar to that of a sports drink. The front label of the bottle displays the word "safe" in four separate locations and only displays "Keep out of the reach of children" as a warning. I believe the shape of the container and the words displayed on the container can mislead people to believe this is a fairly harmless product.

This type of "Gel Fuel" burns very clean, which means it will produce very little to no smoke. It is also possible for this product to burn with very little to no visible flame. Which is what I believe occured during this incident.  I believe it appeared to the one victim that the "Firepot" was out of fuel and no longer burning but in reality there was still a small amount of "Gel Fuel" burning with such a clean burn, there was no visible flame. As the one victim attempted to add "Gel Fuel" to the "FirePot", the opening of the "Gel Fuel" bottle was unknowingly pointed in the direction of the three victims which were seated together. When the open bottle of fuel was placed over what "appeared" to be an extinguished "Firepot", It violently erupted into a ball of fire, spraying the burning "Gel Fuel" all over the deck and victims.

Upon researching this further, I found what appeared to be an identical incident that was reported to have occured in Carlstadt, NJ on June 10th, 2010 in which a 13 year old girl was severely burned.

Please feel free to contact me with any further questions.
justification: Three adults and one child sustained severe burn injuries, with two adults and the child requiring transport to a trauma center.

incident_description:
[REDACTED] (sent to president of JLR Gear),
As per our discussion of today, I have attached several photographs of the propane fire precipitated by the faulty propane meter that I acquired two weeks ago. As I indicated to you in our phone discussion, I was able to determine with a degree of ease that the smoker's regulator was operating normally. However, the packaging on your device indicates that it has a backflow module built into the design. I highly suspect that module failed shortly after I hooked it up and began to preheat the Smoker on May 21st, 2011.  The resulting uncontrolled release of propane superheated the smoker causing a small fire near the ignition source on the deck and at the base of my home. I was forced to quickly put the fire out. At that time, I also was able to determine that the meter  read the propane tank as empty despite the fact that the propane was spewing an uncontrolled temperature fire from the smoker. I shut the valve off at the propane tank and quickly put the fire out. The next day, I inspected the propane tank and was able to determine it was still at or near FULL...thus indicating the propane meter was defective. I gingerly hooked up the propane tank to the smoker propane regulator and tested it to 200 deg for 1 hour and found that it was functional without your propane meter being connected. All of this obviously means your propane gage is defective and likely has a faulty back flow module.
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident involved a significant fire, making it an 'Incident, No Injury' (Severity Level 2). The likelihood of occurrence is 'Possible' (Likelihood 3) given the identified faulty propane meter and backflow module.

incident_description:
I am writing to explain why I think the EPA has created an large environmental hazard in their attempt to eliminate a relatively minor one.

Specifically I am writing about the BLITZ 5-GAL GASOLINE TANK, MODEL 5CXG.

A little backgroundÃÂ I am 68 years of age and in good health, except for a bad back.  I am a homeowner who has used 2 and 3 gallon red gas cans since I was a boy to store gasoline for lawn mowers and yard tools in the summer, and for snow blowers in the winter.  Sure, I might have spilled a few drops in my time, but no more, and I never blamed it on the tanks.

Last fall (2010) I went to buy new gas tanks, and all I could buy were the new ones which I was told ÃÂmet the new EPA standards.ÃÂ  They cost at least twice as much as the old ones, but I want to protect the environment, and I did not complain.

However, when I went to use the new tank on our snowblower, I spilled more gas than ever in my life!  It was nighttime, at the end of a blizzard with a foot of snow around me, when the snowblower ran out of gas.  I got out the new tank to pour some gas, but nothing happened.  After some futzing around outside, in the dark freezing night with my gloves off, I took the tank into the lighted garage to try to figure out how it worked.  I could not get it to work.  I spilled quite a bit trying, but it only dribbled out.  Fortunately my neighbor had some gas in an old, user-friendly tank and I got through the job.  I got through the winter by pouring from the 5-gallon EPA tank into an old usable 2-gallon tank, and then using the old one when needed in action.

This spring I had similar problems in daylight when I tried to use the EPA approved tank on my lawnmower.  I could see how I had to hold the can upright, hold back a locking lever, and depress a handle, and then I could lift the heavy tank (with my 3rd arm) and get the gas to dribble out at a barely acceptable rate (much slower than the old vented tanks.)  By the time it was finished, I had probably spilled about a half a pint of gas, and my back was killing me.

Today, I decided to pour the remaining 3 gallons into my car's gas tank, which is at least waist high, meaning I did not have to lean over. It took a long time (maybe 3 minutes) to release the gas, and I never could get the last pint out of the can.  I had the tube fully inserted into my car's gas tank, but it was leaking from the top of the tube, down the finish of my brand new car, onto the floor of my garage.  Probably lost about a pint.  As I write, my garage is now filled with gas fumes, and I am leaving the door open so we don't have an explosion.

I have had it!  This is an abomination, probably brought to us by the bureaucratic cousins of the designers of hard-to-open drug bottles!  I can't believe anyone ever tried this idea under real conditions before mandating it; it must have been done from behind a desk.

I don't blame the manufacturer.  I blame the people who impose these ridiculous rules.  I am writing to express my own frustration, which must be also held by thousands of other victims of this dumb situation.  I am also concerned about the environment, and this is FAR MORE POLLUTING than any gas tanks I have every used in 6 decades.

I hope this feedback gets passed on to someone who will take us back to a cleaner, cheaper, simpler, and more useable gas can.

Sincerely,
[REDACTED]
Needham, MA
justification: While no injuries were reported, the incident of spilling significant amounts of gasoline due to the new EPA-approved tank's design poses a high likelihood of future incidents.

incident_description: This is about a 5 gallon gas can.  I noticed that every time the weather warmed up my garage would fill with gasoline fumes.  Upon checking, I found wet gasoline on the outside of the container and on the surface on which it sat.  Fortunately, no fire occurred.  The design includes a breather tube that extends from the cap into the can.  Even with the level of gasoline in the can below the full mark, the breather tube is below the fluid level.  When the temperature warms, the expansion of the gasoline and air in the can forces the liquid up the breather tube to the cap and nozzle area where it leaks out due to pressure in the can.  In the picture you can see the wet gasoline on the outside of the can as a shiny area below the filler cap.  Tightening the cap does not prevent the leak.  Also, the can is very poorly designed for handling while transferring fuel from the can.  One hand is required to lift the can.  One hand is required to hold open the mechanism to pour gasoline.  But since the handle for lifting does not extend around the side of the can to be able to tilt the can for pouring, ANOTHER hand is needed to tilt the can somehow.  Most humans have only two hands, making the job of lifting, tilting and opening the can all at the same time very awkward, if not impossible.  This product is clearly poorly designed and dangerous.
justification: Although no injury or fire occurred, the incident involved a hazardous material (gasoline) leaking due to design flaws, posing a potential fire risk.

incident_description:
Purchased a battery powered siphon pump (part number DH-20) distributed by World Marketing of America, Mill Creek, PA. from Home Depot today.  This was for transfer of kerosene from 5 gallon can to  kerosene heater.   Turned the pump on and fuel started to flow. Turned the pump off and fuel continued to flow at same rate even though the switch was turned off.  Confirmed that the motor had stopped pumping, but the siphon action did not stop the flow of kerosene.    I had to quickly pinch the filler hose to mostly stop the flow of kerosene, then quickly remove the hose from the kerosene heater and lift the hose higher than the filler can before the siphon action stopped.  A small amount of kerosene was spilled.   I thought this may have been a one-time-event, so I placed a catch pan under a 2nd kerosene heater and got a clamp to (substantially) stop the fuel flow in case this happened again.  I turned the pump on briefly to start the flow of kerosene, then immediately turned the pump off.  The kerosene continued to flow at the same rate even with the switch turned off.   (The motor was not powered on.)   I quickly clamped the filler hose mostly closed and lifted the hose higher than the filler can.  Again, a small amount of kerosene was spilled. 

I have been using a battery powered siphon pump for kerosene for the past 40 years, so I am very familiar with how they should operate.  

The packaging states "Applicable Liquids:  kerosene, diesel, light oils, water (non-drinkable) and other non-flammable liquids".   
This product is an extreme fire hazard in that the siphon will not stop when the switch is turned off.  

I immediately got on the internet and wrote a complaint to the distributor and told them that this product is unsafe and must be removed from the market.  I also told the distributor that I was going to report this product to the CPSC.    Product will be returned to Home Depot today and the Home Depot manager will be notified about this very unsafe product.
justification: The product's continuous siphoning after power-off poses a significant fire risk, as demonstrated by kerosene spills in two consecutive tests.
